doc.title: Orrin Evans interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 22, 2018

chapter: Early listening and the road not taken
title: Relating to show tunes and buying Kind of Blue
summary: He connected to jazz through tunes he knew; Kind of Blue was his first jazz record, via modes, and he loved Blue in Green.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: That attachment to show tunes and tunes that are melodic and easily remembered, does that affect your own composition? Do you think about the audience and what are they hearing.

Well I think the other tunes are extremely melodic and easy to digest too. I just didn’t know how to do that at that young age. So, and it was more, sorry, it was less about it being easy to digest and more about me just being able to relate to it. You know, or could make a connection. So when I see Coltrane does “My Favorite Things” I say oh wow, and I go and check out, you know, like from the movie. You know what I mean? Or “All the Things You Are” and I’m like okay I know that, and I can apply it. So that was more that kind of thing. And then as time went on and my ears developed — well they’re still developing — but my ears developed and I’ve said okay well let me try this. You know? And then I learned okay, this is what it is and that was probably “Kind of Blue.” That was the first quote unquote jazz record I bought. You know it was definitely — there were some other ones but that was the one like I took a risk. Because there were no standards

on it, I didn’t know anything on it. But I was relating it to modes. We were studying modes in school, in high school, or in middle school around that time, I said grab this record. So for me it was always just being able to connect it to something until I got older and I’m like I don’t need to connect this I just need to enjoy what it is.
Was there a particular tune on “Kind of Blue” that you latched on to?
Most people probably would not pick that one.
Yeah. That did for me one because of the intro and two, it’s a very simple but complex harmonic progression in that tune. So I’ve always, I still love it, I still love it.
